papers.title: MEO: Mining Reliable Expert Signals for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Wireless Networks
papers.summary: The operation of next-generation wireless networks increasingly hinges on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize critical network decisions. Offline RL trains agents using accessible datasets and thus eliminates costly online interactions, rendering it particularly advantageous in dynamic wireless environments that demand low latency and high safety. However, its capability remains under-explored in wireless settings, where offline data are often limited and subject to partial observability. papers.title: Localizing and Editing the Goal Representation of a Vision-Language-Action Model: code
papers.summary: Code and analysis outputs for the paper Localizing and Editing the Goal Representation of a Vision-Language-Action Model (SPAIS Workshop at the 10th Conference on Robot Learning, CoRL 2026). The code studies OpenVLA-7B fine-tuned on LIBERO-Goal. It labels the goal that each closed-loop rollout executes, tests negated and redirected instructions, localizes the goal with activation patching, edits it with patches and steering vectors, and evaluates goal read-outs as runtime monitors.

papers.title: Proof-of-Concept End-to-End EEG-BCI Pipeline for Grasp-and-Release Decoding and Low-Cost Tendon-Driven Actuation
papers.summary: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term motor disability, inspiring research in the design of assistive and rehabilitation technologies that work in situations with limited residual muscle activity. Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising non-muscular pathway to translate brain activity into BCI commands. This paper presents the proof-of-concept end-to-end pipeline for the use of binary grasp-and-release Electroencephalography-Brain Computer Interface (EEG-BCI) decoding in conjunction with low-cost tendon-driven robotic hand actuation. papers.title: Foundation Model-Aided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Wireless Random Access Network Optimization
papers.summary: Random access (RA) is one of the most foundational medium access control (MAC) layer scheduling schemes for handling unpredictable data traffic from multiple terminals. While multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been explored to optimize RA-based wireless networks, its reliance on experience-driven, distributed policy learning incurs significant training overhead for each optimization task, limiting its feasibility in real-world applications. papers.summary: Abstract Reliability engineers in operating facilities are increasingly burdened by the manual aggregation of asset health data from disparate sources — process historians, ERP systems, and periodic inspection records — leaving limited capacity for higher-value analysis and decision-making. This paper presents the design and first deployment of an integrated autonomous inspection and asset performance management solution at a Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) facility, delivered through a tripartite collaboration between KOC, SLB and ANYbotics. papers.summary: Abstract Modern machine control systems rely on GNSS-based positioning integrated with onboard tilt and inertial sensors to enable high-precision excavation, grading, dredging, and earthmoving operations. However, dependence on satellite-derived position and heading limits operational continuity in environments where GNSS signals are degraded or unavailable. papers.title: Advanced Tank Maintenance Technologies in Oil and Gas – Upstream: Robotic De-Sludging, Robotic Coating Removal, Dehumidification, and Drone-Based Inspection for Storage Tank Maintenance
papers.summary: Abstract Extended tank outages remain a persistent constraint on upstream field economics, since a drained storage tank that cannot be returned to service quickly translates directly into lost or deferred production. This paper evaluates four maintenance technologies that Petroleum Development Oman PDO introduced to shorten outage windows and reduce confined-space risk during tank cleaning, surface preparation, coating, and inspection: a remotely piloted hydraulic dozer for bottom-sludge removal, a magnetically mounted climbing robot for coating and Glass-Reinforced Epoxy (GRE) stripping, a co

papers.title: Next-Gen Smart Robotic Repair for Aging Subsea Pipelines
papers.summary: Abstract Offshore operators worldwide are managing subsea pipeline networks that are advancing well into the latter stages of their design lives, where corrosion-driven wall loss competes directly with the cost and disruption of full replacement. This paper reports an application by ADNOC Offshore of an autonomous, diver-free robotic composite repair on a live 20-in. crude oil pipeline, completed with the line in full operation and without a single diver entering the water. papers.title: Transforming UWILD Through Asset-Deployed Robotic Phased Array Corrosion Mapping
papers.summary: Abstract Underwater Inspection in Lieu of Dry Docking (UWILD) enables floating offshore assets to satisfy structural-integrity requirements while remaining in operation. Conventional UWILD ultrasonic examinations, however, commonly depend on diver-deployed point thickness measurements or remotely operated vehicle systems supported by specialized offshore infrastructure. These methods can constrain inspection coverage, positional repeatability, data density, and campaign flexibility. papers.title: Reinventing TRSV Intervention: How Rigless E-Line Robotics Eliminated an Expensive Workover, A Case Study
papers.summary: Abstract Maintaining well integrity throughout the life of a well is essential to preventing uncontrolled flow, enabling the longevity of mature assets, protecting the environment, and safeguarding personnel. Tubing-Retrievable Safety Valves (TRSVs) constitute a primary well-integrity barrier, and malfunction can lead to immediate production impairment and elevated operational risk. papers.summary: BACKGROUND: The role of minimally invasive robotic heart surgery in the surgical field is swiftly expanding due to technological advancements and the acknowledgment that its safety is comparable to conventional cardiac surgery. papers.title: Detection and Recognition of Road Signs by a Computer Vision System Using the YOLO Convolutional Neural Network
papers.summary: Abstract A new version of a neural network model for detecting and recognizing road signs in images and video files using the YOLO convolutional neural network is presented. Based on an analysis of literature sources, the choice was made in favor of using the YOLOv11m convolutional neural network, developed by Ultralytics, in the created system. papers.title: Dynamic Asset Allocation with Direct Policy Optimization: Evidence from a US Public-Market Multi-Asset Universe
papers.summary: This manuscript considers an asset allocation problem where funds must be allocated to 6 broad classes of assets: equity, corporate bonds, government bonds, real estate, gold, and other commodities. papers.summary: This paper investigates the Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) framework under individual penalty constraints to address resource allocation challenges in dynamic wireless networked environments. papers.summary: Long-term orbital missions require highly independent life-support systems, maintaining ecological stability under limited external support and subsystem attenuation. Conventional strategies are typically based on fixed threshold rules or deterministic mass-balance models and cannot adapt to disturbances or multi-objective trade-offs between resource safety and environmental load. papers.summary: Abstract Objectives/Scope Oil & gas operations require continuous monitoring of safety compliance and high risk anomalies; however, conventional supervision and manual CCTV monitoring are constrained by limited coverage, delayed detection, and inconsistent enforcement. This paper presents an AI-based industrial safety monitoring framework for edge computer vision analytics and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to enable real-time detection of safety violations and hazardous conditions. papers.summary: Abstract At remote oil and gas facilities, closed-circuit television still relies on a person watching live views and searching stored footage after an event. papers.summary: Computer vision and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used in industrial Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) management to detect missing personal protective equipment (PPE), restricted-zone entries, and line-of-fire exposure. papers.title: Spontaneous neuropathic pain
papers.summary: Spontaneous pain is a highly prevalent and disabling consequence of neuropathic disorders, yet it remains mechanistically underdefined and therapeutically underserved. Historically, preclinical animal models and clinical trials have been overwhelmingly biased toward stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity, relegating spontaneous pain to a secondary manifestation.
